result.summary: The pedestrian environment is largely unprotected, lacking marked crosswalks, traffic control devices, and ADA-compliant curb ramps. The industrial setting and presence of parked vehicles create sightline issues and a generally hostile atmosphere for walking.

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection
hazards.description: The lack of crosswalk markings fails to designate a safe path for pedestrians or alert drivers to their presence.

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Control
hazards.description: No stop signs or signals are visible to regulate vehicle speeds or right-of-way at the intersection.

hazards.name: Poor Sidewalk Condition
hazards.description: Cracks and overgrown vegetation on the sidewalk present tripping hazards.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style crosswalk markings to improve visibility and define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Construct concrete curb ramps with truncated domes to provide accessible transitions from sidewalk to street.

interventions.title: Corner Radii Reduction
interventions.description: Tighten the corner curb to slow turning vehicles and shorten the pedestrian crossing distance.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential intersection with row houses and a one-way street configuration. The environment lacks basic pedestrian infrastructure such as marked crosswalks, curb ramps, and pedestrian signals, while parked vehicles near the corner create significant sightline obstructions.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the intersection, providing no designated space or visual cue for pedestrians to cross.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles located very close to the intersection corner block the view between approaching drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The absence of sloped curb transitions makes the intersection inaccessible for people with mobility aids or strollers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and physically prevent parking too close to the intersection.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install standardized curb ramps with detectable warning surfaces at all crossing points.

result.summary: The environment is a residential corner with continuous sidewalks and a modern curb ramp featuring tactile paving. Pedestrian safety is primarily compromised by significant sightline obstructions from a vehicle parked directly at the corner and the use of low-visibility transverse crosswalk markings.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: A large black pickup truck is parked immediately adjacent to the crossing area, blocking the view between pedestrians and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground at the street corner

hazards.name: Low-Visibility Crosswalk
hazards.description: The existing crosswalk markings are faded and consist of thin parallel lines, which are less visible to approaching drivers than high-visibility patterns.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the side street in the foreground
